sections.overview: Lethrinus enigmaticus Smith, 1959 is a western Indian Ocean emperor, with records from the Seychelles and Saya de Malha Bank.
sections.identification: The body is bronze or grey, often lighter below; dark purple spots mark the lower eye rim, and the maxilla is reddish. It reaches about 55 cm total length.
sections.habitat: It lives over seagrass beds, coral reefs and nearby sand, to about 50 m deep.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on echinoderms, crustaceans and fish, with molluscs also recorded.
sections.behavior: The species accounts consulted give little detail on its social behaviour beyond its habitat and feeding observations.
sections.reproduction: A spawning peak was recorded in October at Saya de Malha, but the study did not sample every part of the year; females there were smaller and more numerous than males.
sections.ecology: It was once synonymized with Lethrinus mahsena, but the FAO catalogue treats the Blackeye emperor as distinct based on its characteristic colour and combination of traits.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists a 2009 IUCN assessment of Least Concern; the assessment is old and does not describe present local abundance.
